title: Generative AI as a partner for teachers in building personalised learning paths for students with ease in Tanzania
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can help secondary school teachers in Tanzania design personalised learning paths more efficiently and effectively. The motivating problem is that large class sizes, limited teaching resources, and uneven access to training make it difficult for teachers to differentiate instruction, provide timely feedback, and manage workload while still meeting diverse learner needs.

The study evaluated generative AI tools, especially ChatGPT and Grok, in support of lesson planning, assessment creation, adaptive content delivery, and student feedback. The sample included 120 secondary school teachers from public schools in Dar es Salaam and Dodoma, representing both urban and rural contexts. The paper combined surveys, classroom/perception data, and student outcome measures; it reported pre/post comparisons of engagement, completion, test scores, and attendance, along with teacher perceptions of usability and workload reduction.

Findings suggest that generative AI was perceived as easy to use, helpful for reducing workload, and effective for tailoring instruction to student needs. The study also reports improved student engagement and academic performance after AI integration. However, it highlights that insufficient training and weak infrastructure, especially in rural areas, limit adoption. The paper concludes that generative AI can function as a supportive partner for teachers, but only if paired with professional development and better digital infrastructure.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/LLM system used to generate text and support instructional tasks such as lesson planning, quizzes, and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Used alongside Grok and other generative AI tools to help secondary school teachers in Tanzania create personalised learning paths, including lesson plans, quizzes, student feedback, and adaptive content.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that AI-supported approaches improved adaptability to individual learning needs (mean 4.5 vs 2.5 under traditional methods) and timely feedback and assessment (mean 4.6 vs 2.6). The paper also reports improved student engagement (2.8 to 4.3) and mean test scores (61% to 75%) after generative AI integration, but these results are presented across the AI tools rather than isolated for ChatGPT alone.
findings.measure: Teacher-rated adaptability and feedback; student engagement; mean test scores

identified_tools.name: Grok
identified_tools.description: xAI's generative AI chatbot/LLM system designed for conversational assistance and reasoning-based text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used with ChatGPT by secondary school teachers in Tanzania for lesson planning, assessments, and adaptive content delivery to create personalised learning paths.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers using generative AI reported higher ease of use (M=4.3 vs 3.1 for non-experienced teachers) and greater helpfulness in reducing workload (M=4.1 vs 2.9). The paper attributes these advantages to generative AI use overall, not to Grok separately, so no tool-specific effect size is reported.
findings.measure: Ease of use; workload reduction; content adaptation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods, single-study evaluation with surveys, pre/post comparisons, and t-tests rather than a randomized controlled design. It provides empirical evidence, but the report does not isolate tool-specific causal effects and relies heavily on teacher perceptions.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are substantial at the combined generative-AI level, including student engagement increasing from 2.8 to 4.3 and test scores from 61% to 75%. However, because the paper does not provide tool-specific effect sizes and blends multiple AI tools, the impact is best treated as modest-to-strong but not precisely attributable to one product.
